faq.a: Sharif is associated with the Arabic form شَرِيف, whose core sense is sharif; noble, honourable.

faq.q: What is the origin of Sharif?
faq.a: Sharif is associated with Arabic. Sharif is Arabic شَرِيف (Sharīf), meaning 'noble, honourable'.
Yes — the underlying form شَرِيف is Arabic.
Sharif can occur in Muslim naming contexts, but it is better described as a Arabic-origin name used within some Muslim naming traditions than as an exclusively Islamic religious term.
Sharif should not be classified as a Quranic personal name without a direct Quranic basis. The root ش ر ف is Quranic, but Sharīf is not itself a Quranic personal name.

faq.q: What does Sharif mean in Urdu?
faq.a: In Urdu, Sharif is rendered شریف and carries the sense شریف، بزرگ.

faq.q: What does Sharif mean in Persian?
faq.a: In Persian, Sharif is rendered شریف and carries the sense شریف، نجیب.
A romanized syllable approximation is sha-rif. No IPA transcription is asserted because a verified phonetic transcription was not available.

faq.q: What are the variants of Sharif?
faq.a: Romanization variants include Sharif, sharif. Script forms are شریف, شَرِيف, शरीफ़.

faq.q: Is Sharif a boy's or girl's name?
faq.a: Documented usage records this form as male. Gender is not inferred from the meaning of the word, and actual use may vary between communities.
